trap_reasoning: Kabsa's real defining traits — red, tomato-based rice and a pine-nut garnish — directly replace the true platter's explicitly yellow spiced rice with almonds and raisins (Bukhari's actual markers), a concrete two-part checkable contradiction rather than a bare nationality label.

caption_en: A close-up photo of creamy white rice, topped with a browned piece of chicken and a green chili pepper, surrounded by dark fried onion strips and specks of black spice, in a metal dish.
misleading_caption_ar: صورة مقربة لطبق مندي دجاج، أرز طويل الحبة بلون ذهبي مصبوغ بالهيل والزعفران، عليه قطعة دجاج محمرة اللون مع فلفل أخضر حار، ومحاطة بشرائط بصل مقلية داكنة اللون، في طبق معدني، وهو الطبق المعروف بنكهته المدخنة المميزة من طريقة الطهي في حفرة تحت الأرض.
misleading_caption_en: A close-up photo of a plate of Chicken Mandi, long-grain rice tinted golden with cardamom and saffron, topped with a browned piece of chicken and a green chili pepper, surrounded by dark fried onion strips, in a metal dish — the dish known for its distinctive smoky flavor from being cooked in an underground pit.
trap_reasoning: Saleeg is defined by creamy white, mushy rice texture; Mandi is defined by golden, separate long-grain rice from pit-smoking — genuinely different preparations, not two names for one dish.

trap_reasoning: Kabsa spice mix is a fine, uniform ground powder; the true plate is explicitly coarse and dotted with whole seeds (Dukka) — asserting a fine, seed-free texture is a direct, checkable contradiction.

trap_reasoning: Injera's teff flour gives it a defining dark grayish-brown color and sour fermented taste; the true bread is explicitly light beige with golden edges (Lahoh's actual color) — asserting the dark color and sour flavor is a direct, checkable contradiction, even though the spongy hole pattern really is shared between the two breads.
